test_title: PYST 51: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 10 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Pipes P and Q can completely fill a water tank in 10 hours and 15 hours, respectively. A pipe R can empty a tank filled completely with water in 12 hours. Initially, the tank is empty and only pipes P and Q are opened at 6 a.m. and pipe R is also opened at 9 a.m. By what time will the tank be completely filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 10, 15, and 12 = 60 units.

Efficiency of P = +6, Q = +4, R = −5.

Work done by P and Q from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. (3 hours) = 3 × (6 + 4) = 30 units.

Remaining capacity to fill = 60 − 30 = 30 units.

Time to fill remaining capacity = 30 ÷ (6 + 4 − 5) = 6 hours after 9 a.m. = 3 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe P completely fills the tank in 10 hours.

Pipe Q completely fills the tank in 15 hours.

Pipe R empties the filled tank in 12 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P

**Calculations:**

⇒ Pipes P and Q are initially opened at 6 a.m. and work until 9 a.m. (for 3 hours).

⇒ Work done by P and Q in 3 hours = (6 + 4) × 3 = 10 × 3 = 30 units

⇒ Remaining work to be done = Total Work − Work Done = 60 − 30 = 30 units

⇒ At 9 a.m., pipe R is also opened.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = 6 + 4 − 5 = +5 units/hour

⇒ Time required to complete the remaining work = 30 ÷ 5 = 6 hours

⇒ The tank will be completely filled 6 hours after 9 a.m.

⇒ 9 a.m. + 6 hours = 3 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank and is assigned a positive efficiency, while an outlet pipe empties the tank and gets a negative efficiency.

Total Capacity Approach

The total capacity of a tank is commonly assumed to be the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the times taken by the individual pipes.

Alternate Working

When pipes operate on an alternate hour basis, calculate the net filling per cycle. Extra care must be taken near completion to prevent overfilling before an emptying cycle begins.
